experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Trek through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and glacial moraines while witnessing stunning 360-degree views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. This is the crown jewel of the region and a bucket-list experience for any trekker.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most celebrated sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges in a breathtaking panorama. The short but rewarding hike takes about 1.5 hours from Ghorepani village and is suitable for most fitness levels.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and raw Himalayan beauty without the crowds of the main ABC route. Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests to High Camp at 3,580m, with jaw-dropping close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna massif.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Walk in Ghandruk
experiences.description: Spend a day exploring Ghandruk, one of the largest Gurung villages in Nepal. Walk through traditional stone-paved lanes, visit the Gurung Museum to learn about indigenous culture and customs, interact with locals, and enjoy authentic dal bhat and raksi (local millet wine) at a family-run teahouse. A perfect blend of nature and cultural immersion.

experiences.name: Jhinu Danda Natural Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: After days of strenuous trekking, reward your tired muscles with a rejuvenating soak in the natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river near Jhinu Danda. The geothermal pools sit beside a rushing glacial river surrounded by lush forest, creating a magical and restorative natural spa experience unique to this region of the Annapurnas.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, exchange currency at airport (avoid hotel exchange rates). Take a prepaid taxi or public bus to Thamel district (budget ~500-700 NPR for taxi). Check into a budget guesthouse in Thamel, rest and freshen up. Walk around Thamel to get oriented, pick up any last-minute trekking gear from local shops at negotiable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Thamel's vibrant streets. Visit a local gear shop to finalize equipment rentals (trekking poles, sleeping bag liner if needed). Explore Asan Bazaar nearby for authentic local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Quick dal bhat or momos at a local Thamel eatery (~300-400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat set meal at a local Thamel restaurant such as OR2K or a similar budget spot (~400-600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and orientation. Confirm your TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) requirements. TIMS costs ~2000 NPR and ACAP ~3000 NPR for foreigners - obtain these in Kathmandu before heading to Pokhara.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Swayambhunath Stupa (Monkey Temple) for sunrise views over Kathmandu Valley (~200 NPR entry). Explore the stupa complex and surrounding shrines. Grab TIMS card and ACAP permit from Nepal Tourism Board office in Thamel (bring passport photos and copies of passport).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kathmandu bus station and take a tourist bus or local bus to Pokhara (7-8 hours, ~800-1500 NPR for tourist bus vs ~400 NPR local bus). Enjoy scenic mountain views along the highway. Arrive in Pokhara in the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget guesthouse near Lakeside area in Pokhara. Walk along Phewa Lake promenade. Explore Lakeside street for budget gear shops and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Bread, eggs, and tea at a Thamel bakery (~200-300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at a roadside dhaba during bus journey (~200-300 NPR)
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant - try local trout or dal bhat (~400-600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Obtain all permits in Kathmandu before departing. Keep multiple passport photo copies handy. Tourist buses are more comfortable but local buses are significantly cheaper.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning rowboat on Phewa Lake to Barahi Temple island (~500 NPR for boat rental, shareable). Watch sunrise reflecting off Annapurna and Machhapuchhre peaks from the lake. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic mountain views - hike up takes about 45 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local jeep or bus from Pokhara to Nayapul (2-3 hours, ~300-500 NPR). This is the starting point of the Annapurna Circuit and Sanctuary treks. Register permits at the checkpoint in Birethanti. Begin trekking from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga or Hile (approximately 3-4 hours of moderate trekking, 1,540m elevation).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tikhedhunga or Hile. Check into a basic teahouse (~500-800 NPR per night). Rest tired legs and socialize with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara guesthouse breakfast - eggs, toast, tea (~250-350 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Birethanti (~400-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner - dal bhat, vegetable curry (~400-600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season in Nepal - weather is generally clear and dry. Book teahouses in advance or arrive early. Carry a headlamp, water purification tablets, and layers for cooler evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00-6:30 AM) for sunrise mountain views from the teahouse. Begin trekking from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri - this involves a famous steep stone staircase of approximately 3,300 steps (challenging but rewarding). Take breaks and enjoy rhododendron forests along the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,874m). The trail winds through beautiful forests with increasing mountain views. Total trekking time from Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani is approximately 5-6 hours. Arrive in Ghorepani by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ghorepani village. Acclimatize to the altitude (2,874m). Watch sunset over Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges from Ghorepani. Warm up by the teahouse fire with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs with tea at Tikhedhunga teahouse (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Snack break at Ulleri - local noodle soup or snacks (~300-400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Ghorepani teahouse (~500-700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The Ulleri staircase is one of the most demanding sections of the early trek. Pace yourself and stay hydrated. Altitude sickness can begin above 2,500m - watch for headaches or nausea.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake up at 4:30-5:00 AM to hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. The 45-minute hike rewards with panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and over 20 Himalayan peaks. Entry fee ~100 NPR. Photograph the golden hour light on the peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast, then begin trekking toward Tadapani via Deurali. The trail passes through beautiful rhododendron and oak forests. Trek takes approximately 4-5 hours. Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m) by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Tadapani teahouse. Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. The village is smaller and more peaceful than Ghorepani.

meals.breakfast: Post-Poon Hill breakfast at Ghorepani - eggs, toast, hot porridge (~350-450 NPR)
meals.lunch: Light snack or noodle soup on the trail (~300-400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Teahouse meal - try local Nepali thali at Tadapani (~500-700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill sunrise is a highlight of the entire trek - do not miss it. Bring warm layers as it is extremely cold before dawn at this altitude. Carry a good camera or ensure phone is charged.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre from Tadapani. Begin trekking from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m) - a descent of approximately 4-5 hours through dense forests. Cross suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river. Chhomrong is the last major village before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong. Explore this picturesque Gurung village with its terraced fields and traditional stone houses. Visit the local monastery. Chhomrong offers the last reliable mobile network and ATM access before the sanctuary - withdraw cash as teahouses inside the sanctuary are cash only.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse in Chhomrong with views of Annapurna South directly ahead. Prepare gear for the deeper trek into the sanctuary. Socialize with trekkers at the teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and eggs at Tadapani (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse between Tadapani and Chhomrong (~400-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Chhomrong teahouse dinner - fresh vegetables and rice (~500-700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Withdraw sufficient cash in Chhomrong as there are no ATMs beyond this point. Teahouse prices increase significantly inside the sanctuary. Budget approximately 1,000-1,500 NPR per day for food inside the sanctuary.

day_by_day.morning: Begin trekking from Chhomrong toward Himalaya Hotel via Sinuwa and Bamboo. The trail descends steeply to the Modi Khola river then climbs through bamboo and rhododendron forests. This section is known for leopard and red panda sightings (rare but possible). Trek is approximately 4-5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Himalaya Hotel to Dovan (2,600m) or push on to Machapuchare Base Camp approach. The valley narrows dramatically as you enter the Annapurna Conservation Area inner sanctuary. Towering walls of Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre rise on either side. Arrive at Dovan or Hinku Cave area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a basic teahouse at Dovan. The facilities become more basic inside the sanctuary but the scenery more dramatic. Enjoy the incredible stargazing at this altitude away from light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Chhomrong teahouse - eggs, chapati, tea (~350-450 NPR)
meals.lunch: Snack stop at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse (~400-600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Teahouse meal at Dovan - dal bhat or pasta (~600-800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Prices inside the sanctuary are higher due to the remote location. Dal bhat is always the best value option. The trail can be slippery with morning frost in October - use trekking poles.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m. The trail ascends through increasingly dramatic alpine scenery. Views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) become overwhelming as you approach MBC. Trek takes approximately 4-5 hours. Acclimatize slowly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest at Machhapuchhre Base Camp. Short acclimatization walk around the area. Stunning 360-degree views of Machhapuchhre, Annapurna III, Gangapurna, and Hiunchuli. Continue to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m if feeling strong (additional 1.5-2 hours). Arrive at Annapurna Sanctuary - the Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Check into your accommodation at Annapurna Sanctuary (Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay). Celebrate reaching ABC. Watch the alpenglow on Annapurna I (8,091m), the 10th highest mountain in the world, turning golden and pink at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Dovan teahouse - porridge and hot tea (~400-500 NPR)
meals.lunch: Snack at MBC - hot soup and snacks to warm up (~500-700 NPR)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at ABC accommodation to celebrate arrival (~800-1,200 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness is a real concern at 4,130m. Symptoms include headache, nausea, dizziness, and shortness of breath. Descend immediately if symptoms are severe. Acclimatize properly - do not rush. Drink plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake up for the most spectacular sunrise of the trek. Watch the first light hit Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Annapurna III, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre simultaneously. The entire amphitheater of peaks glows in shades of orange, pink, and gold. Photograph extensively from different angles around the base camp area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full exploration day at Annapurna Base Camp. Take short walks around the sanctuary bowl. Visit the memorial area dedicated to climbers who lost their lives on Annapurna. Learn about the history of Annapurna expeditions - it was the first 8,000m peak ever climbed (1950, French expedition). Rest and acclimatize.
day_by_day.evening: Second sunset at ABC - equally spectacular. Stargazing at 4,130m with minimal light pollution offers extraordinary views of the Milky Way. Socialize with fellow trekkers from around the world at the teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Post-sunrise breakfast at ABC accommodation - eggs, porridge, hot drinks (~500-700 NPR)
meals.lunch: Light snacks and soup at the teahouse (~400-600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or noodle soup at ABC accommodation (~800-1,000 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Spend two nights at ABC to fully acclimatize and enjoy the experience. October weather is generally stable but afternoon clouds can roll in - mornings offer the clearest views. Keep warm - temperatures at night can drop to -10°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise at Annapurna Base Camp. Take last photographs of the amphitheater of peaks. Begin descent from ABC (4,130m) back toward Machhapuchhre Base Camp and continue to Bamboo or Sinuwa. Descent is significantly faster than ascent - approximately 4-5 hours to Bamboo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending through the bamboo and rhododendron forests. The descending trail offers new perspectives on the landscape. Arrive at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse by early afternoon. Legs will feel the steep descent.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse. Celebrate the successful trek to ABC. Enjoy a warm meal and rest aching muscles.

meals.breakfast: Final ABC breakfast - make it a good one (~500-700 NPR)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks or quick stop at MBC (~400-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Hearty teahouse meal at Bamboo - dal bhat with extra rice (~500-700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Descent can be hard on knees - use trekking poles and take your time on steep sections. Knees and quads will be sore. The descent from 4,130m to lower altitudes will feel much warmer and more comfortable.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back to Chhomrong (approximately 3-4 hours). The trail climbs back up the steep steps to Chhomrong village. Enjoy the terraced village and Gurung culture. Visit the Chhomrong monastery if time permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Chhomrong toward Jhinu Danda (1,780m) - a 1.5-2 hour descent. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola river. Soak tired muscles in the natural hot springs (~200-300 NPR entry).
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening relaxing at Jhinu Danda teahouse. The hot springs can be visited again in the evening. Enjoy the lower altitude warmth after days at high elevation.

meals.breakfast: Bamboo teahouse breakfast (~350-450 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Chhomrong (~500-600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at Jhinu Danda - fresh vegetables and rice (~500-700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a well-deserved reward for trekkers. They are located a 20-minute walk below the village. Bring a towel and flip-flops. The springs are natural and very relaxing for tired muscles.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda to Nayapul (approximately 4-5 hours). The trail follows the Modi Khola river valley through Landruk and Tolka villages. Enjoy the lower altitude subtropical vegetation, terraced rice paddies, and traditional Gurung villages. This is a beautiful and relatively easy section.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul. Take a local jeep or bus from Nayapul back to Pokhara (1.5-2 hours, ~300-400 NPR). Arrive in Pokhara by early afternoon. Check into a Lakeside guesthouse. Take a long hot shower - the first proper one in days!
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek with a lakeside dinner. Stroll along Phewa Lake promenade. Enjoy Pokhara's vibrant Lakeside atmosphere with restaurants, cafes, and shops.

meals.breakfast: Jhinu Danda teahouse breakfast (~350-450 NPR)
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Nayapul before the bus (~300-400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a Lakeside restaurant - treat yourself to something special (~600-1,000 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The return to Pokhara marks the end of the main trekking section. Treat yourself to a celebration meal. Many trekkers get a massage in Pokhara to recover tired muscles - budget massages available from ~500-800 NPR per hour.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Get a budget massage or Ayurvedic treatment for sore muscles (~500-800 NPR). Visit the International Mountain Museum to learn about Himalayan climbing history (~400 NPR entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a rowboat on Phewa Lake to Barahi Temple island (if not done on Day 3). Alternatively, rent a bicycle and cycle around the lake (150-200 NPR per hour). Visit the Devi's Fall waterfall and Gupteshwor Cave (~100 NPR each). Explore the old Pokhara Bazaar for local handicrafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara. Watch sunset from the Lakeside with views of the Annapurna range - now familiar peaks after your trek. Visit a rooftop restaurant for panoramic mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara bakery breakfast - fresh pastries, coffee (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Local Newari or Gurung restaurant for authentic cuisine (~400-600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant with mountain views - try local fish (trout) or momos (~500-800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara has excellent budget options for massage and recovery. The International Mountain Museum is highly recommended for context on the peaks you just visited. Sort and back up all your trek photographs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal. Wake up early for last views of the Annapurna range from Pokhara. Take a tourist bus or local bus back to Kathmandu (7-8 hours, ~800-1,500 NPR tourist bus). Alternatively, take a domestic flight Pokhara to Kathmandu (30 minutes, ~5,000-8,000 NPR - worth it if time is short). Enjoy the scenic Prithvi Highway journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kathmandu. Visit Boudhanath Stupa (one of the largest stupas in the world, ~400 NPR entry) or Pashupatinath Temple (Hindu cremation temple on the Bagmati River, ~1,000 NPR entry for non-Hindus). Last-minute souvenir shopping in Thamel - bargain hard for pashminas, Thangka paintings, and handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kathmandu at a rooftop Thamel restaurant with mountain views. Pack bags for departure. Reflect on an incredible 14-day Annapurna adventure. Head to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara guesthouse breakfast before departure (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Roadside dhaba on the highway or airport restaurant (~300-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Thamel rooftop restaurant - splurge slightly on last night (~600-1,000 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Kathmandu airport check-in. Traffic in Kathmandu can be very heavy - plan accordingly. Keep trekking permits and entry receipts as souvenirs. Total estimated budget for the 14-day trip excluding international flights: approximately USD 400-600 (NPR 55,000-80,000) covering accommodation, food, transport, and permits.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Kathmandu to Pokhara via private tourist bus or shared jeep (approximately 6–7 hours) or take a 25-minute domestic flight to Pokhara if budget allows. Settle into a lakeside guesthouse in Pokhara for the night before heading toward Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Phewa Lake promenade in Pokhara. Enjoy the calm lakeside atmosphere, browse local shops, and watch the sunset over the Annapurna range from the lakeside.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at Kathmandu airport
meals.lunch: Quick dal bhat or momos at a local eatery near Kathmandu airport before departure
meals.dinner: Lakeside Restaurant, Pokhara — try Nepali thali set or grilled fish from Phewa Lake (mid-range, ~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your domestic Pokhara flight in advance if preferred over the bus. Confirm your trek permits (ACAP and TIMS) can be arranged in Pokhara the next morning. Keep energy levels in mind after a long travel day.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning in Pokhara — visit the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) office and TIMS office to collect your trekking permits. Take a short walk to the World Peace Pagoda for panoramic Annapurna and Dhaulagiri views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours by local bus or jeep), then begin trekking to Tikhedhunga (1,540m). The trail passes through terraced rice fields, rhododendron forests, and traditional Gurung villages. Trek duration: approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tikhedhunga teahouse. Relax on the terrace, enjoy mountain views, and socialize with fellow trekkers. Acclimatize gently to the altitude.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara guesthouse breakfast — eggs, toast, and tea (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Birethanti or along the trail (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Tikhedhunga — vegetable curry, rice, and lentil soup (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — teahouses will be busy. Book ahead if possible. Carry a daypack with essentials; a porter can be hired in Nayapul for ~$15–20/day.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Tikhedhunga. Climb the famous stone staircase (over 3,000 steps) ascending to Ulleri (2,073m). The climb is steep but rewarding with sweeping valley views and dense rhododendron forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Ulleri through Banthanti to Ghorepani (2,874m). The trail levels out through beautiful forest. Arrive at Ghorepani by early afternoon and check into your teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk to the lower viewpoint near Ghorepani for Annapurna South and Dhaulagiri views. Return for a warm dinner and rest — tomorrow requires a very early start.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or pancakes at Tikhedhunga teahouse before departure (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Ulleri or Banthanti teahouse (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Ghorepani teahouse — garlic soup, dal bhat, and apple pie (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Tikhedhunga to Ulleri staircase is one of the toughest sections of the Annapurna Circuit. Pace yourself and stay hydrated. Altitude is increasing — drink plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike (depart 5:00–5:30 AM) to Poon Hill (3,210m) — one of the most iconic sunrise viewpoints in Nepal. Watch the sunrise paint Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Dhaulagiri, Machapuchare, and over a dozen Himalayan peaks in golden light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast, then trek onward through Deurali to Tadapani (2,630m). The trail passes through magnificent rhododendron and oak forests with occasional Himalayan wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Tadapani teahouse. Enjoy the quieter, less-crowded atmosphere compared to Ghorepani. Star-gazing from the terrace on clear October nights.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea at Poon Hill summit, then full breakfast back at Ghorepani teahouse — eggs, toast, porridge (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Snack pack or light meal at Deurali (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Tadapani teahouse — pasta, vegetable curry, or dal bhat with hot ginger tea (~$7–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headlamp and warm layers for the Poon Hill sunrise hike — temperatures can drop to near 0°C at dawn in October. The Poon Hill entry fee is included in your ACAP permit.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (2,170m) — a beautiful descent and ascent through forest and terraced farmland. Chomrong is a large Gurung village and the last major settlement before the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chomrong village — visit the local gompa (monastery), interact with Gurung families, and enjoy sweeping views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). Check into your teahouse and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Annapurna South from Chomrong's terraces. Evening tea and conversation with local teahouse owners about Gurung culture and traditions.

meals.breakfast: Tadapani teahouse — muesli with milk, eggs, and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or soup at a teahouse along the Tadapani–Chomrong trail (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Chomrong teahouse — try the local Gurung bread (sel roti) if available, with vegetable curry and soup (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong has the last reliable ATM and phone signal before the Sanctuary. Withdraw sufficient cash here. Stock up on snacks and any medications needed for higher altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Chomrong early and descend to the Chomrong Khola river, then climb steeply to Sinuwa (2,360m). The trail enters the Annapurna Conservation Area more deeply, with dense bamboo and rhododendron forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through Kuldi and Bamboo (2,310m) to Dovan (2,600m). The gorge narrows dramatically as you enter the Modi Khola valley. Watch for Himalayan tahr, langur monkeys, and colorful Danphe pheasants.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Dovan teahouse. Enjoy the dramatic gorge scenery and the sound of the Modi Khola river rushing below. Rest well — altitude is increasing steadily.

meals.breakfast: Chomrong teahouse — pancakes with honey, boiled eggs, and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Bamboo teahouse — noodle soup or fried noodles (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dovan teahouse — dal bhat set meal (the most nutritious and filling option at altitude) (~$7–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Teahouse options become more limited from here. Menus are standardized and prices increase slightly with altitude. Avoid raw vegetables and stick to cooked meals to prevent stomach issues.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan through Himalayan (2,920m) and Hinku Cave to Deurali (3,230m). The gorge becomes increasingly dramatic with waterfalls, hanging glaciers visible above, and the trail often hugging cliff faces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the final push from Deurali to Machapuchare Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m). The landscape transforms dramatically — vegetation thins and the massive walls of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and the sacred Machapuchare tower above.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Machapuchare Base Camp. Acclimatize, hydrate well, and enjoy the extraordinary mountain amphitheater. Watch the alpenglow on Machapuchare at sunset — one of Nepal's most breathtaking sights.

meals.breakfast: Dovan teahouse — porridge with dried fruit and hot lemon tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Himalayan or Hinku Cave teahouse — simple soup and bread (~$6–8 USD)
meals.dinner: MBC teahouse — dal bhat or pasta, hot chocolate or ginger lemon honey tea (~$8–11 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude at MBC is 3,700m — altitude sickness symptoms (headache, nausea, dizziness) can occur. Ascend slowly, drink 3–4 liters of water daily, and do not ascend if feeling unwell. Carry altitude sickness medication (Diamox) as a precaution.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start (5:00 AM) from MBC — trek the final 2 hours to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m) for sunrise. The 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare is absolutely overwhelming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at ABC — explore the base camp area, take photographs, and soak in the extraordinary high-altitude environment. Check into the Annapurna Sanctuary / Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay for your overnight.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC — watch the last light fade on the Annapurna massif. The silence and scale of the mountain amphitheater at dusk is deeply moving. Warm dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and energy bars on the trail to ABC; proper breakfast after arrival (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: ABC teahouse/boutique stay — soup, bread, or dal bhat (~$8–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Boutique Stay, ABC — hearty dal bhat, pasta, or available set menu with hot drinks (~$10–14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trip. At 4,130m, cold temperatures are expected even in October (can drop to -10°C at night). Wear all your layers. Altitude sickness risk is real — if symptoms worsen, descend immediately. Do not sleep higher than you feel comfortable.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise at Annapurna Base Camp — a quiet, reflective morning in one of the world's most spectacular mountain settings. Take a short exploratory walk around the base camp perimeter to view the glacial moraines and ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC to Bamboo (2,310m) — a long but mostly downhill day. The descent covers approximately 1,800m in altitude. Enjoy the changing landscape as vegetation returns and temperatures warm.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo teahouse. Celebrate reaching ABC with a well-earned rest. Legs will be tired — stretch thoroughly and stay hydrated.

meals.breakfast: ABC Boutique Stay — porridge, eggs, and hot tea before descent (~$6–8 USD)
meals.lunch: Dovan or Himalayan teahouse — noodle soup or fried rice (~$6–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Bamboo teahouse — dal bhat or pasta with hot chocolate (~$7–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The descent from ABC to Bamboo is long (5–7 hours). Use trekking poles to protect your knees. Start early to avoid arriving after dark. October days are shorter than summer months.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back through Sinuwa to Chomrong (2,170m). The trail through the bamboo and rhododendron forest feels different on the way back — notice details missed on the ascent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest afternoon in Chomrong. Optional: visit the Chomrong Khola hot spring area (small natural springs below the village) or explore the upper Gurung village and monastery at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Chomrong — you've successfully completed the Annapurna Sanctuary trek. Share stories with fellow trekkers over apple brandy (local specialty) if desired.

meals.breakfast: Bamboo teahouse — muesli, eggs, and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Sinuwa teahouse — dal bhat or fried noodles (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Chomrong teahouse — special dinner: try buff (water buffalo) steak or mixed vegetable curry with apple pie for dessert (~$9–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Phone signal returns at Chomrong — check in with family and friends. You can also arrange a porter or additional guide here if needed for the remaining trek days.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong back toward Jhinu Danda (1,760m) — a shorter, pleasant trail descending through terraced fields. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs on the Modi Khola riverbank.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs (small entry fee ~$2–3 USD) — a perfect reward for tired trekking legs. The springs are set beside the rushing river with mountain views. Spend 1–2 hours relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Continue or stay overnight at Jhinu Danda. Alternatively, push on to New Bridge and up to Landruk (1,565m) for a different return route through Gurung villages.

meals.breakfast: Chomrong teahouse — pancakes with honey and tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Jhinu Danda teahouse — soup and sandwiches by the hot springs (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Jhinu Danda or Landruk teahouse — dal bhat or pasta (~$6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu hot springs are a beloved highlight of the return route. Go early in the afternoon before they get crowded. The springs are naturally warm but not scalding — very relaxing after days of trekking.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Landruk (or Jhinu) to Tolka and then Dhampus (1,650m) — a beautiful ridge walk with continuous panoramic views of the Annapurna range. October clarity makes this one of the finest viewpoints of the entire trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Dhampus and explore this traditional Gurung village. Visit the local school if open, interact with villagers, and photograph the beautifully terraced hillsides. Check into a teahouse with Annapurna views.
day_by_day.evening: Final Himalayan sunset of the trek from Dhampus ridge — Annapurna South, Machapuchare, Hiunchuli, and Mardi Himal all visible. A deeply satisfying conclusion to the trekking journey.

meals.breakfast: Landruk/Jhinu teahouse — eggs, toast, and porridge (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Tolka teahouse — noodle soup or fried rice (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dhampus teahouse — celebratory dal bhat with local raksi (rice wine) or masala tea (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Dhampus is accessible by road from Pokhara — arrange a jeep pickup for the next morning. This is your last night on the trail. Reflect on the incredible journey through the Annapurna Sanctuary.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise from Dhampus with the full Annapurna panorama. Pack up and take a jeep or local bus back to Pokhara (1–1.5 hours). Check into a comfortable lakeside hotel in Pokhara — enjoy a hot shower and real bed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon in Pokhara to decompress. Options include: boat ride on Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi Temple island, visit the International Mountain Museum (highly recommended, ~$5 entry), or simply relax at a lakeside café.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Pokhara to mark the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek. Explore the Lakeside (Baidam) restaurant strip and enjoy a well-deserved feast.

meals.breakfast: Dhampus teahouse — final trail breakfast (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Pokhara lakeside café — fresh salad, pizza, or continental meal (first non-teahouse meal in days!) (~$7–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Moondance Restaurant or Caffe Concerto, Pokhara — wood-fired pizza, pasta, or Nepali cuisine in a nice setting (~$12–18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Treat yourself to a massage in Pokhara — many excellent Ayurvedic and traditional Nepali massage centers along the lakeside charge ~$15–25 for a full-body session. Laundry services are also widely available.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Pokhara. Optional sunrise visit to Sarangkot viewpoint (30-minute drive/hike) for one last Annapurna panorama — or sleep in and enjoy a relaxed breakfast by Phewa Lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Pokhara to Kathmandu — by domestic flight (25 minutes, ~$80–100 USD) or tourist bus (6–7 hours). If time permits in Kathmandu, visit Thamel for last-minute souvenir shopping or a quick visit to Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Kathmandu — farewell dinner in Thamel. Reflect on 14 extraordinary days in the Annapurna region. Prepare for departure or onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara lakeside hotel — full breakfast with fresh fruit, eggs, and good coffee (~$5–8 USD)
meals.lunch: En route meal or Kathmandu café — try Newari cuisine (bara, yomari) for a cultural farewell (~$6–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Thamel House Restaurant, Kathmandu — traditional Nepali set dinner with cultural dance performance (~$15–20 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your ACAP and TIMS permits as souvenirs — they make great mementos. If departing Nepal imminently, confirm your international flight details. Kathmandu airport recommends arriving 3 hours before international departures.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — private luxury transfer awaits with a dedicated concierge to assist with luggage and documentation
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter transfer from Kathmandu to Pokhara or nearest helipad serving the Modi Khola Valley, offering breathtaking aerial views of the Himalayan foothills. Check in to the Annapurna Sanctuary Boutique Stay, settle into your premium suite, and enjoy a welcome orientation with the lodge manager
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the lodge terrace with panoramic views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). Light welcome cocktails and canapés served by personal butler

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Premium in-flight dining or a curated arrival snack platter at the lodge upon check-in featuring local cheeses, Nepali pickles, fresh fruit, and herbal teas
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the lodge featuring a multi-course Nepali tasting menu — dal bhat royale with organic lentils, butter-poached chicken sekuwa, saffron kheer, and locally sourced seasonal vegetables, paired with premium Himalayan spring water and imported wines

day_by_day.notes: Acclimatization is essential. The lodge sits at approximately 4,130m (Annapurna Base Camp area). Spend the first evening resting, hydrating well, and avoiding strenuous activity. A lodge physician or wellness advisor will conduct a brief altitude health check upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle acclimatization walk around the Modi Khola Valley floor — a guided nature trail lasting 2–3 hours exploring rhododendron forests, glacial moraines, and alpine meadows. Expert naturalist guide explains local flora, fauna, and geology. Elevation gain kept minimal
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided photography session capturing the iconic Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheater — Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Machapuchare framing the glacier. Return to lodge for a luxury spa treatment: Himalayan hot stone massage using locally sourced heated stones and yak butter balm
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing session with a private astronomer guide — the Sanctuary's remote location offers extraordinary dark skies. High-powered telescopes provided. Warm yak wool blankets and hot buttered rum served

meals.breakfast: Lavish lodge breakfast buffet — freshly baked Nepali breads, eggs cooked to order, Tibetan butter tea, fresh-pressed juices, granola with local honey, seasonal fruit platter, and smoked meats
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic lunch enjoyed on the trail — artisan sandwiches, quinoa salad, Nepali achar, premium energy bars, thermos of hot soup, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at the lodge — interactive five-course dinner featuring Himalayan trout ceviche, wild mushroom risotto with truffle oil, slow-braised yak tenderloin, and cardamom panna cotta. Paired with curated Bordeaux selections

day_by_day.notes: Drink at least 3–4 liters of water today. Avoid alcohol consumption until fully acclimatized (typically 48 hours post-arrival at altitude). The lodge's altitude wellness kit includes Diamox (available on request), oxygen canisters, and pulse oximeters.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise trek to Annapurna Base Camp viewpoint (if staying in the Sanctuary) — depart at 05:30 for a guided 2-hour ascent to catch the golden alpenglow on Annapurna I. Expert mountain guide leads the way with full safety equipment. Return to lodge by 09:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural immersion walk to a nearby Gurung or Magar village — visit traditional stone houses, interact with local families, witness weaving and farming traditions. Private cultural interpreter accompanies. Lodge arranges respectful community contribution
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Nepali cultural evening at the lodge — private Gurung cultural performance featuring Rodhi songs, Ghatu dance, and traditional musical instruments. Followed by a bonfire gathering

meals.breakfast: Pre-trek energy breakfast at 05:00 — warm porridge with Himalayan berries, boiled eggs, Tibetan bread with yak butter and honey, and ginger lemon tea. Full hot breakfast served upon return
meals.lunch: Village-style lunch prepared by a local family — authentic dal bhat, gundruk soup, seasonal saag, and homemade yogurt. A premium donation is made to the host family
meals.dinner: Bonfire dinner under the stars — Nepali BBQ featuring marinated lamb chops, corn on the cob, roasted potatoes, and freshly baked Tibetan bread. Locally brewed raksi (millet wine) and imported craft beers available

day_by_day.notes: October is peak autumn trekking season in Nepal — expect crystal-clear skies and ideal temperatures (0°C to 15°C at altitude). Layers are essential. The cultural village visit requires respectful attire — the lodge provides guidance on appropriate dress.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium guided trek — descend from the Sanctuary toward Deurali and Himalaya Hotel area, exploring the dramatic Modi Khola gorge. Towering canyon walls, cascading waterfalls, and dense bamboo forests create a spectacular natural corridor. Trek distance: approximately 8–10 km
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trek through rhododendron and oak forest zones. Naturalist guide identifies Himalayan bird species including Danphe (Himalayan Monal — Nepal's national bird), blood pheasants, and lammergeiers. Reach a premium rest camp for afternoon refreshments
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge via private jeep or horseback (guest preference). Lodge offers a recovery hydrotherapy session — Himalayan salt bath, aromatherapy steam room, and deep tissue sports massage

meals.breakfast: Full American-style lodge breakfast — fluffy pancakes with maple syrup, smoked salmon, avocado, fresh-pressed orange juice, and specialty Nepali single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch at a scenic overlook — thermos of pumpkin bisque, smoked chicken wraps, energy trail mix, premium chocolate, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Intimate lodge dinner — slow-roasted Himalayan lamb with rosemary jus, roasted root vegetables, truffle mashed potatoes, and a decadent chocolate fondant with Himalayan sea salt caramel sauce

day_by_day.notes: This is a moderately strenuous trekking day with significant descent. Trekking poles are provided by the lodge. Altitude decreases as you descend, which aids acclimatization. Porter service included — guests carry only a light daypack.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated birdwatching and wildlife morning — expert ornithologist guide leads a 3-hour early morning excursion through the forest zones surrounding the lodge. Target species include Himalayan Monal, satyr tragopan, snow partridge, and various raptors. Premium binoculars and field guides provided
day_by_day.afternoon: Watercolor or photography masterclass — resident artist or professional photographer leads a 2-hour creative workshop capturing the Annapurna landscape. All materials provided. Finished artwork framed as a luxury keepsake
day_by_day.evening: Private yoga and meditation session on the lodge's mountain-view deck — certified Himalayan yoga instructor leads a 90-minute restorative session incorporating pranayama breathwork, yin yoga, and guided meditation aligned with Buddhist mountain traditions

meals.breakfast: Lighter wellness breakfast — acai bowl with granola and local honey, green smoothie, poached eggs on sourdough, herbal detox tea blend
meals.lunch: Lodge garden-to-table lunch — fresh salads with local greens, lentil soup, whole grain flatbreads, grilled paneer, and seasonal mountain vegetables
meals.dinner: Fusion fine dining experience — chef presents a creative blend of Nepali and European cuisine: Himalayan herb-crusted sea bass (flown in from Kathmandu), saffron risotto, and a deconstructed mango lassi dessert. Premium wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: A rest and rejuvenation day designed to balance the physical demands of trekking. Guests are encouraged to use the lodge's wellness facilities — spa, library, and meditation garden — at leisure. Altitude wellness check conducted by lodge staff.

day_by_day.morning: Guided high-altitude flora trek — botanist-led exploration of the unique alpine ecosystem surrounding the Sanctuary. Discover rare Himalayan medicinal plants including yarsagumba (cordyceps fungus), Himalayan edelweiss, primulas, and gentians. Comprehensive field notes provided
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter scenic flight over the Annapurna massif — private 45-minute luxury helicopter tour circling Annapurna I, II, III, IV, and Gangapurna. Pilot provides expert commentary. Exclusive aerial photography opportunity with professional camera equipment available
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with the lodge's head chef — learn to prepare authentic Nepali dishes including dal bhat, momo dumplings, gundruk ko jhol, and sel roti. Recipes presented in a beautifully bound keepsake cookbook

meals.breakfast: Nepali-inspired breakfast — sel roti with honey, aloo tama (bamboo shoot and potato curry), fresh curd, spiced chai, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: High-altitude picnic at a scenic meadow — gourmet sandwiches, Himalayan cheese board, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and premium thermos beverages
meals.dinner: Feast on the dishes prepared during the cooking class — enjoy your own creations alongside the chef's refinements in an intimate private dining setting. Celebration toast with Himalayan sparkling water and imported Champagne

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter flight is weather-dependent. October typically offers excellent flying conditions with clear skies and stable winds. The lodge will confirm the flight the evening prior. A backup scenic viewpoint hike is arranged if weather prevents flying.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium trek to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) — depart at 06:00 with expert mountain guide and personal porter. The 4-hour ascent through increasingly dramatic alpine terrain offers close-up views of the sacred Fishtail Mountain (Machapuchare, 6,993m), which is off-limits to climbers
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC (3,700m) for lunch and exploration. Spend 2 hours exploring the base camp area, photographing the extraordinary mountain panorama, and absorbing the profound silence and scale of the Himalayan environment. Begin gradual descent
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge by 17:00. Full body recovery spa treatment — 90-minute deep tissue massage, foot reflexology, and Himalayan herbal compress therapy. Private hot tub session with mountain views available

meals.breakfast: High-energy pre-trek breakfast — steel-cut oatmeal with dried fruits and nuts, scrambled eggs with smoked salmon, whole grain toast, fresh juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed at MBC — thermos of hearty minestrone, premium sandwiches, energy bars, dark chocolate, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Celebratory lodge dinner marking the halfway point of the journey — premium tasting menu with wine pairing: amuse-bouche, Himalayan trout tartare, wild mushroom consommé, braised yak short rib, artisan cheese course, and petit fours

day_by_day.notes: MBC sits at 3,700m — guests should be well acclimatized by Day 7. Pulse oximetry checks conducted before departure and upon return. This is the most physically demanding day of the trip. Trekking poles, altitude medication, and emergency oxygen are carried by the guide.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning — gentle 2-hour guided meditation walk along the Modi Khola river bank. The sound of glacial meltwater, alpine birds, and mountain silence creates a deeply restorative experience. Mindfulness practitioner guides breathing and awareness exercises
day_by_day.afternoon: Private fly-fishing experience on the Modi Khola river — expert fishing guide teaches traditional and fly-fishing techniques. The river hosts Himalayan snow trout (Schizothorax). Catch-and-release policy maintained. Premium fishing equipment provided
day_by_day.evening: Astronomy and Himalayan mythology evening — expert guide combines stargazing with storytelling of Nepali and Hindu celestial mythology. The Milky Way is exceptionally vivid at this altitude. Premium telescopes, star charts, and warm beverages provided

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast — eggs Benedict with yak prosciutto, fresh-baked croissants, seasonal fruit compote, premium Nepali coffee, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic lunch — artisan charcuterie board, local cheeses, fresh flatbreads, grilled vegetables, and sparkling water with fresh mint
meals.dinner: Intimate lodge dinner — pan-seared Himalayan trout (if caught), lemon caper butter sauce, saffron pilaf, roasted asparagus, and a warm almond tart with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Day 8 is intentionally designed as a lighter activity day to allow physical recovery after the MBC trek. Guests are encouraged to use the lodge library, journal, or simply rest and absorb the mountain environment. Spa and wellness facilities remain available throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Guided trek to the Annapurna Sanctuary glacier viewpoint — a 3-hour moderate hike to a premium vantage point offering unobstructed views of the South Annapurna Glacier. Glaciologist guide explains the impact of climate change on Himalayan glaciers and the significance of the Sanctuary ecosystem
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter transfer from the Sanctuary to Pokhara — scenic 20-minute flight over the Annapurna range descending to the lakeside city. Check in to a luxury 5-star lakeside resort in Pokhara (Begnas Lake Resort, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge, or equivalent)
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Phewa Lake — private luxury wooden boat with captain. Views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges reflected in the lake. Champagne and canapés served on board. Visit Tal Barahi Temple island by boat

meals.breakfast: Final Sanctuary breakfast — full lodge spread with all signature dishes, fresh-baked goods, and a special farewell tea ceremony with the lodge team
meals.lunch: In-flight snack box during helicopter transfer, followed by a premium welcome lunch at the Pokhara resort — grilled sea bass, Caesar salad, artisan bread, and fresh lemonade by the pool
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the Pokhara resort's signature restaurant — panoramic Annapurna views, curated Nepali-Continental fusion menu, and an extensive wine cellar selection

day_by_day.notes: Transition day from the high-altitude Sanctuary to the lower elevation of Pokhara (820m). Guests may notice significantly warmer temperatures and increased oxygen levels — a welcome change. Luggage is handled entirely by lodge and resort staff.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise paragliding over Pokhara — tandem paragliding flight from Sarangkot Hill with a certified professional pilot. Soar above Phewa Lake with the entire Annapurna range as a backdrop. One of the world's most spectacular paragliding experiences. Premium safety equipment and professional photography package included
day_by_day.afternoon: World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) visit — guided cultural tour of the stunning Buddhist stupa perched above Phewa Lake. Expert Buddhist cultural guide explains the significance of the pagoda and Nepali Buddhist traditions. Followed by a visit to the International Mountain Museum
day_by_day.evening: Lakeside Pokhara dining and exploration — private guided evening walk through Pokhara's Lakeside district. Visit local artisan workshops, browse premium Nepali handicrafts, pashmina, and Thangka paintings. Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before paragliding — yogurt parfait, banana, energy bar, and green tea. Full breakfast served upon return to resort
meals.lunch: Lakeside premium restaurant lunch — wood-fired pizza, fresh pasta, Nepali thali, and fresh lime soda. Scenic Phewa Lake views
meals.dinner: Premium Newari cuisine dinner at a curated Pokhara restaurant — Newari feast featuring bara (lentil pancakes), choila (spiced grilled meat), aloo tama, and yomari sweets. Traditional Newari music performance accompanies dinner

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding is weather-dependent — October is considered optimal season with stable thermals and clear skies. The resort concierge will confirm the flight time the evening prior. Minimum weight 40kg, maximum 120kg. Not recommended for guests with heart conditions or recent injuries.

day_by_day.morning: Begnas Lake kayaking and nature experience — private guided kayaking tour on the serene Begnas Lake, 15km from Pokhara. Surrounded by terraced hills and the Annapurna range, this pristine lake offers exceptional birdwatching and tranquility. Luxury picnic spot arranged on the lake shore
day_by_day.afternoon: Tibetan refugee settlement cultural visit — guided tour of the Tashiling Tibetan refugee camp. Meet Tibetan artisans, observe carpet weaving and Thangka painting, and learn about Tibetan culture and the refugee experience. A meaningful and respectful cultural immersion. Premium purchases support the community directly
day_by_day.evening: Private Ayurvedic wellness evening at the resort — 2-hour Ayurvedic consultation and treatment with a certified practitioner. Includes dosha assessment, abhyanga full-body oil massage, shirodhara (warm oil head treatment), and herbal steam therapy

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — freshly baked pastries, eggs station, tropical fruit platter, smoked salmon, and specialty Himalayan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic at Begnas Lake — premium hamper with smoked meats, artisan cheeses, freshly baked bread, seasonal salads, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining — private table with lake view, seven-course chef's tasting menu featuring seasonal Nepali ingredients elevated with French technique. Sommelier-guided wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Begnas Lake is a UNESCO-recognized wetland of significant ecological importance. The kayaking experience is suitable for all fitness levels. Life jackets and professional guides provided. The Tibetan settlement visit is conducted with full community permission and cultural sensitivity protocols.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ghandruk village — private jeep transfer to the trailhead followed by a moderate 3-hour guided hike to the iconic Gurung village of Ghandruk (1,940m). One of Nepal's most beautiful traditional villages with stone-paved streets, traditional Gurung architecture, and spectacular Annapurna South and Hiunchuli views
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ghandruk — visit the Gurung Museum, interact with local women's cooperatives, observe traditional weaving, and enjoy the village atmosphere. Afternoon guided descent back to the jeep transfer point. Return to Pokhara by 17:00
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail reception at the resort — the resort hosts a private sunset gathering on the terrace. Personalized gifts prepared: a custom Thangka painting commissioned during the trip, a leather-bound trip journal, and a curated Nepali artisan gift hamper

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — full buffet spread to fuel the Ghandruk day trip
meals.lunch: Authentic Gurung lunch at a family-run premium guesthouse in Ghandruk — traditional dal bhat, local chicken curry, fermented vegetables, and homemade raksi. A generous community contribution is included
meals.dinner: Celebration farewell dinner at Pokhara's finest restaurant — Chef's special menu celebrating the journey: Himalayan-inspired amuse-bouche, premium seafood, Wagyu beef tenderloin, and a bespoke dessert crafted to represent the Annapurna skyline in chocolate and sugar

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk is one of the most rewarding cultural experiences in the Annapurna region. The village sits at a comfortable altitude after the high-altitude Sanctuary days. Comfortable trekking shoes required. The lodge at Ghandruk is available for an overnight stay if guests wish to extend, though the itinerary returns to Pokhara.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Pokhara — optional sunrise hot air balloon flight over the Pokhara Valley and Annapurna range (subject to availability and weather). Alternatively, a final guided meditation session at the resort's lakeside pavilion. Unhurried checkout preparation
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Pokhara to Kathmandu — choice of scenic mountain flight (45 minutes, spectacular aerial views) or premium road transfer through the Prithvi Highway along the Trishuli River gorge (6–7 hours, scenic but leisurely). Check in to a 5-star Kathmandu hotel (Dwarika's Hotel, Hyatt Regency, or Soaltee Crown Plaza)
day_by_day.evening: Kathmandu cultural evening — private guided tour of Thamel and the historic core of Kathmandu. Visit Pashupatinath Temple at dusk for the evening aarti ceremony (sacred fire ritual). Followed by a curated Newari cultural dinner in a heritage courtyard setting

meals.breakfast: Final Pokhara resort breakfast — leisurely full spread with all signature items. Farewell tea ceremony with resort staff
meals.lunch: In-transit lunch — premium picnic box for road transfer, or airport lounge dining for mountain flight option
meals.dinner: Heritage Newari dinner in Kathmandu — feast in a restored Rana-era palace or traditional Newari courtyard. Multi-course Newari cuisine with live classical Nepali music. Kukuri rum cocktails and premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The mountain flight from Pokhara to Kathmandu is highly recommended for clear-day views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, Manaslu, and Ganesh Himal. October skies are typically crystal clear. The Pashupatinath evening aarti is a deeply moving spiritual experience — respectful attire required.

day_by_day.morning: Final Kathmandu morning — private guided tour of Boudhanath Stupa (UNESCO World Heritage Site), one of the world's largest Buddhist stupas. Circumambulate the stupa with a Buddhist monk guide, spin prayer wheels, and observe morning puja rituals. Visit a premium Thangka gallery for last-minute curated art acquisitions
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury farewell experience — private visit to Patan Durbar Square (UNESCO World Heritage Site) with expert art historian guide. Explore the finest Newari architecture, ancient temples, and the Patan Museum. Final premium shopping for pashmina, silver jewelry, and Nepali handicrafts at curated artisan boutiques
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation — private luxury transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport with dedicated concierge assistance. VIP airport lounge access arranged. Farewell gift from the travel company: a curated luxury Nepali gift box including premium Himalayan tea, organic honey, handmade paper journal, and a custom map of the Annapurna journey

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast — full international and Nepali spread, freshly baked pastries, eggs station, fresh juices, and specialty Nepali coffee for a memorable final morning
meals.lunch: Premium farewell lunch at a Kathmandu fine dining restaurant — rooftop views of the Kathmandu Valley, curated Nepali-Continental menu, and a toast to the journey with sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium dining — the concierge arranges a special departure meal box with Nepali sweets, premium chocolates, and artisan snacks for the journey home
